# dsh-xwide-handoff
> A **handoff** plugin for **DeepSeek Harness (DSH)**: one `/handoff` turns a nearly-full chat into
a **structured handoff card + a clean new session**, pinned to the top of the sidebar. It can also *
*prepare the next leg automatically** when the context runs hot.
中文说明 · Changelog · MIT License
## The problem
Long tasks fill the context window. DSH's built-in auto-compaction is **lossy** — it eats detail, an
d you are still in the same session, still filling up.
This plugin takes a different route — **handoff**:
1. Write down *where we are* — what was changed, what was verified, what is next — as a **handoff ca
session is **auto-named** (`<original>_01`, `_02`, … from a persistent counter), **auto-pinned** an
d **filed into the source session's project group**.
You changed rooms; the baton did not drop.

## Usage

- Anything after `/handoff` lands in the card's "本次交接重点" section.
- **Omitting it is fine** — the ca

rd still carries "files touched this round" and your last 6 user messages.
- The command reports the
new session id/title and pins it.
**Note**: `/handoff` is a slash command — **only the user can type it**; a model cannot invoke it. T
hat is exactly why the plugin also ships auto-ready (below): at threshold it *prepares* the handoff
xactly why the plugin also ships auto-ready (below): at threshold it *prepares* the handoff for you.
## Auto-ready (`autoReady`)
When enabled, the plugin watches every `turn/end` and reads how much context the last request carrie
en enabled, the plugin watches every `turn/end` and reads how much context the last request carried:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
- **≥ `readyPct` (default 0.7)** → it runs a full handoff: create session, name it, pin it, inject t

he card, and drive its first turn (so it is guaranteed to appear in the sidebar).
- **It does not sw
itch sessions for you** — you click the pinned session. DSH exposes no server-side "switch the brows

er's session" API, and that boundary is intentional.
- Fuses: one prepare per session, global cooldo
wn (10 min default), and the switch defaults to **off**.
> ⚠️ Use `inputTokens`, **not** `usage.totalTokens`. The latter is cumulative spend (we have seen 20
5k) and will trigger on everything.

### `childMode`
| value | behaviour | when |
| `create` | server creates a **fresh empty session** (zero context; inherits cwd + agentPreset) | *

*recommended default**; no client half required |
| `none` | server creates nothing; the card JSON r
ides in the command result and `client.js` creates a **visible** session through the GUI-native API

| when you need the exact "New chat" behaviour; requires `client.js` wired as `dsh.client` |
| `fork
` | inherits the full history (context **not** cleared) | rename-only scenarios |
> ⚠️ None of them may set `parentSession` — DSH excludes sessions carrying `parentSession` from the
list and the recoverable set; that is the classic "handoff finished but no new session shows up" bug

## How it works (for people changing the code)
- **Naming**: sequence numbers come from an on-disk counter (`~/.dsh/named-handoff-counter.json`, bu
cketed per cwd). They are **not** derived from the source title's trailing number — the source sessi
on is always freshly opened with no such suffix, so that approach always yields `_01`. The name list

lives in `~/.dsh/named-handoff-names.json`.
- **Three pinning channels**: ① the card's first line i
s the target title (the built-in title service reads it); ② `ctx.sessions.using(...).binding.session

.rename()` (absent on some builds); ③ `session.append("session/title", …)`.
- **Self-heal re-pin**:
the official title service deliberately overwrites pinned titles ("overwriting a pinned user title i

s the point"), so the plugin watches title events and re-pins names it owns (up to `repinLimit`).
-
**`prompt` needs a signal**: `sessionController.prompt(request, signal)`'s wrapper calls `signal.thr

owIfAborted()` on its first line — pass `new AbortController().signal`.
- **`blank` only flips on `t
urn/start`**: the sidebar filters `blank: true` sessions out entirely (and renders them as "New sess
ion"). Injecting a message does not flip it — you must actually drive a turn.
## Compatibility
This plugin uses **DSH internals** (not a stable public contract), verified against:
| What | Where |

| `sessionController.prompt / create / resolveAgent` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-api-session-controller` |
|
`session.append` `surfaceOp` semantics | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session` (`SURFACE_EVENT_TYPES` = system

/developer/user/assistant/message + tool/result) |
| `system/message` must be the first surface node

| `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-format-v3-to-v4` `foldSurface()` |
| `workspaceRegistry.pinSession` | `

@deepseek-ai/dsh-workspace` |
| `projectController.baseline / assign` | `dsh-project-groups` (**opti

onal**; skipping when absent) |
| sidebar `blank` filter | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace` |
**Re-check this table after upgrading DSH.** Every internal call degrades gracefully: failures are l
ogged, never fatal to the handoff.
